items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: Interviewer mentions: 'I've heard, gone to listen to Archibald a lot... I don't know if he was playing around when you were. I don't know. I know the name, but I don't know why.' Interviewee does not confirm any personal interaction or relationship with Archibald.

ctx.x: your own feelings. You don't think it can be done. You do the best you can, but you're stuck with some of it. Yeah, but you can sure tell something for motor reaction, if nothing else. Yeah, you can tell, yeah, you certainly can tell a lot. You just can't separate it out too precisely.

Yeah. The applause, things like that. Well, and I've heard, gone to listen to Archibald a lot, he used to play just off, wherever you know St. Peter the piano player, the guy who made Stackely, I don't know if he was playing around when you were. I don't know. I know the name, but I don't know why. Anyway, he played solo piano a lot. I'd go and listen to him. When the crowd was right, the barmaid would say, well how come you don't play like this for us? Well I mean it does make a difference when people appreciate…

say this since it gives me a chance to, and it's something you and I have moaned about for years. Really, it really irritates me to an extreme when you get an audience that applauds after every solo. Yeah. Well, it messes the next soloist up. It sure does. Or it would seem to me it would. Yeah. Never heard a musician comment on this. No. But from the standpoint of people who are really
